tasks.title: A rolling deployment
tasks.statement: Right now a new version is deployed to all servers at once: the service is unavailable during the deployment. Switch the strategy to “one at a time (rolling)” and choose the number of servers so that during an update (minus one server) the remaining ones can handle 1300 requests per second. The design must survive a deployment. The budget is $700 per month. The “Deployment” parameter is shown in this exercise.
tasks.hint: Three M servers: during an update two remain — 1400 requests. Two servers are too few: one would remain (700).

tasks.title: When there is no headroom
tasks.statement: The fleet is small — two M servers (1400 requests), and the load is 1300. A one-at-a-time deployment would leave one server, which is not enough, and the budget does not allow buying a third. Choose blue/green: capacity does not drop during the deployment. At most two servers, load at most 95%, and cost of at most $700 per month (blue/green doubles the server spend).
tasks.hint: The server’s “Deployment” parameter is blue/green. Server spend is then ×2: 2 × 240 = 480.

tasks.title: Which is cheaper: rolling or blue/green
tasks.statement: The load has grown to 6000 requests per second, and blue/green is currently in use: server spend doubles. Compare the prices: with a large fleet, rolling is noticeably cheaper. Switch the deployment to “one at a time” and choose the number of servers: the design survives a deployment, load is at most 90%, and the budget is $2200 per month.
tasks.hint: Ten M servers: during a deployment nine remain — 6300 requests. Blue/green with nine servers would cost 2160 for servers alone — too expensive.

tasks.title: A deployment and a zone failure
tasks.statement: The servers must survive both a deployment (minus one server) and a zone failure (minus a third). The load is 2000 requests per second. Place the servers across three zones, enable rolling, and choose the number of servers: the design survives a deployment, a zone failure and a server failure.
tasks.hint: Four M servers: after losing a zone two remain — 1400, too few. Five: after losing a zone three remain — 2100, and during a deployment four — 2800.

tasks.title: Safe delivery
tasks.statement: The chapter's final exercise. A shop: 2500 requests per second, with a cache and a database. Build a design that survives a deployment (rolling), a zone failure, and failure of the database and the cache, with monitoring: load at most 80%, budget $3000 per month.
tasks.hint: Seven M servers (after losing a zone five remain — 3500); a cache with a replica in three zones; an M database with a replica and automatic failover in three zones; monitoring.
